newsitem.title: USA: Maine works on damage estimates after big storm.
newsitem.headline: Maine works on damage estimates after big storm.

text.p: Maine, which was hit hard by a big storm over the weekend, said initial reports show there was around $10 million of damage, but it still is working on more detailed estimates for the three counties struck the hardest.

"We're using the figure of $10 million as a very, very ballpark figure, but until we get a little more hard data from teams we won't have any more hard data than that," said Lynette Miller, a senior manager of the state Emergency Management Agency.
Maine, which declared a state of emergency for three southern counties on Monday, has said it expects the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to begin making its assessment on Wednesday.
Should FEMA agree that the damage is sufficiently severe to qualify for federal aid, Gov. Angus King expects to ask President Bill Clinton to issue a Declaration of Disaster on Thursday or Friday.

Portland, which suffered some heavy flooding, still has roads shut, the state emergency official said, adding that state employees in the area were told not to report to work until noon, partly due to problems with the water system.

Portland residents have been told to boil their water as they wait for crews to finish repairing a pipeline that carries water to the city from Sebago Lake, she said. "They're slowly getting back to normal," Miller said.
However, there were no reports of any damage to pipelines that carry natural gas or crude oil, she added.
